prompt.context_jp: 京橋庵とのコラボ企画は、S&Fの食品事業を立て直すための切り札であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 京橋庵とのコラボ企画___、S&Fの食品事業を立て直すための切り札であった。

feedback.correct_en: The collaboration project is established as the topic of the opening sentence — は frames it as 'as for this project' so the predicate can characterize it.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as new information in a presentational sense, but here the narrator is setting up the topic for commentary, not introducing it as a newly spotted entity.

contrast_examples.en: This project is the trump card. (topic)
There is a trump card. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 京橋庵からは専務の磯川が先着し、静かに書類を開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 京橋庵からは専務の磯川___先着し、静かに書類を開いた。

feedback.correct_en: Isozawa is introduced here as new information — the person who arrived first. が presents him into the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Isozawa had already been established as the topic, but this is his first appearance in the narrative.

contrast_examples.en: As for the executive, he came. (already known)

prompt.context_jp: ソバーガーは彼が押し切って通した目玉であり、後には引けない。
prompt.prompt_jp: ソバーガー___彼が押し切って通した目玉であり、後には引けない。

feedback.correct_en: Soburger is the topic being characterized here; は sets it up so the clause can describe what it means to Asano.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as new-info subject, but the sentence is commenting about an already-mentioned project.

prompt.context_jp: 会場の空気は既に張り詰めている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会場の空気___既に張り詰めている。

feedback.correct_en: The atmosphere is the topic whose state is being described — は marks the topic of 張り詰めている.
feedback.incorrect_en: を marks a direct object; 張り詰める here is intransitive, so を is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: 空気は張り詰めている。

prompt.context_jp: 言葉が滑り出す前の一瞬、耳の中で自分の鼓動だけが鳴っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 耳の中で自分の鼓動だけ___鳴っていた。

feedback.correct_en: だけ+が gives the exhaustive sense: 'only his heartbeat (and nothing else) was ringing'. が is standard with だけ in this exhaustive-listing use.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to a contrastive 'at least his heartbeat', changing the nuance away from the intended 'only'.

prompt.context_jp: 時計の針が、無言で背中を押した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の針___、無言で背中を押した。

feedback.correct_en: The clock hands appear as a new, dramatic agent in this scene — が introduces them as the thing acting on him.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the clock hands a continuing topic, but this is a vivid, momentary image, not an ongoing subject.

prompt.context_jp: あれは 昨日の段階で 捨てた企画なので あのままです
prompt.prompt_jp: あれ___昨日の段階で捨てた企画なので、あのままです。

feedback.correct_en: あれ refers to a shared, known item (the discarded proposal) being discussed — は topicalizes it to explain its status.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as newly identified, but both speakers already know which proposal is meant.

contrast_examples.en: That one is old. (comment on known thing)
That one is the good one. (exhaustive pick)

prompt.context_jp: 数字の裏付けも、言葉の運びも、隙が無い。
prompt.prompt_jp: 数字の裏付けも、言葉の運びも、隙___無い。

feedback.correct_en: 〜がない is the standard existential negation: 'there is no gap'. が marks the thing whose existence is denied.
feedback.incorrect_en: を can't appear with ない (adjective-like negative existence); it's ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: プレゼンは 派遣の仕事ではございません
prompt.prompt_jp: プレゼン___派遣の仕事ではございません。

feedback.correct_en: Omae is making a general statement about presentations as a category — 'as for presentations, (they) are not a temp's job'. は marks the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify which specific thing is not a temp's job, but she's categorically defining the scope of her duties.

contrast_examples.jp: それは私の仕事ではない。

prompt.context_jp: 直した企画書の内容を把握してるのは大前さんしかいません。大前さんが適任なんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 大前さん___適任なんです。

feedback.correct_en: Satonaka is singling Omae out as THE right person — exhaustive-listing が ('Omae and no one else is the right fit').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would merely topicalize Omae and lose the emphatic 'only she is right for this' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: As for him, he's the culprit. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 京橋庵の伝統は 石臼びきの 蕎麦粉を使った十割蕎麦ですが
prompt.prompt_jp: 京橋庵の伝統___石臼びきの蕎麦粉を使った十割蕎麦ですが…

feedback.correct_en: The tradition is the topic being characterized, and the 〜ですが sets up an implicit contrast with the new product — は carries both topic and contrastive weight.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify which thing is the tradition, but here she's commenting about Kyobashi-an's known tradition.

contrast_examples.jp: 伝統は十割だが、今回は違う。
contrast_examples.en: The tradition is 10:0, but this time is different. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 一方 ワサビなどの薬味は 希望する客への オプション提供とし コスト削減いたします
prompt.prompt_jp: 一方、ワサビなどの薬味___希望する客へのオプション提供とし、コスト削減いたします。

feedback.correct_en: 一方 (on the other hand) sets up explicit contrast with the previous point about packaging — contrastive は is the correct marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply identify a subject and lose the contrast signaled by 一方.

contrast_examples.jp: 肉は食べるが、魚は食べない。
contrast_examples.en: I eat meat, but not fish. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: たった今 京橋庵から連絡がありました
prompt.prompt_jp: たった今、京橋庵から連絡___ありました。

feedback.correct_en: 連絡がある is the existential 'there was contact (just now)' — brand-new information being reported to the boss, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the contact was already known and being commented on, contradicting 'just now'.

contrast_examples.en: As for calls, yes there were. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 派遣には 会社の責任は 取れませんが 派遣にだって 取るべき責任はあります
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣には会社の責任___取れませんが、派遣にだって取るべき責任はあります。

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: 'company responsibility — THAT a temp can't take, but...' setting up the contrast with the second clause's 取るべき責任はあります.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply identify the object but lose the parallel contrast structure between the two clauses.

contrast_examples.jp: 酒は飲むが、たばこは吸わない。
contrast_examples.en: I drink alcohol, but don't smoke. (contrast は)

prompt.context_jp: 浅野は思わず、隣の宇野に肘で合図を送った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 浅野は思わず、隣の宇野に肘___合図を送った。

feedback.correct_en: 肘で = 'with his elbow' — で marks the instrument used to signal.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make the elbow the direct object of 送る, which doesn't fit the meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 前回の企画書から 適度な修正 出過ぎない改善を加えて ___
prompt.prompt_jp: 適度な修正、出過ぎない改善を加えて___みました。

feedback.correct_en: まとめる = 'to put together, compile' is the standard collocation for finishing a proposal document.
feedback.incorrect_en: 固める and つめる don't collocate naturally with 企画書 in this 'finalize the write-up' sense.

prompt.context_jp: よろしいんですか？ 派遣に責任は___が
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣に責任は___ませんが。

feedback.correct_en: 責任を取る ('to take/accept responsibility') is the fixed collocation. The potential form 取れません means 'cannot take'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 責任を持つ exists but means 'to be in charge of'; here Omae specifically rejects the ability to assume accountability, which is 取る.

prompt.context_jp: 会長不在のまま、商談は___としていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 商談は___ようとしていた。

feedback.correct_en: 〜ようとしていた with intransitive 始まる expresses 'was about to begin' from the event's perspective.
feedback.incorrect_en: 始めよう is the volitional of transitive 始める, which would need an agent subject. 始まり is a noun form that doesn't fit the grammar.

contrast_examples.jp: 試合が始まろうとしていた。
contrast_examples.en: The match was about to begin.

contrast_examples.jp: 試合を始めようとした。

prompt.context_jp: 塵も積もれば___となるとばかりに、小さな修正を丹念に重ねていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 塵も積もれば___となる

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piled up becomes a mountain') is a fixed proverb meaning small things add up.
feedback.incorrect_en: The proverb uses 山, not 川 or 海 — this is a fixed set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a mickle makes a muckle.
A journey of 1000 ri starts with one step.

prompt.context_jp: 千葉は差し出された封筒を両手で受け取り、深々と___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 深々と___。

feedback.correct_en: 深々と一礼する is a set collocation describing a deep, formal bow.
feedback.incorrect_en: 挨拶する and 返事する don't naturally take 深々と as a modifier — only physical bowing does.

prompt.context_jp: 大前さん ありがとうございました → 「大したことは ___ が」
prompt.prompt_jp: 大したことは___おりませんが。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the appropriate humble verb form.

feedback.correct_en: 大したことはしておりません is Omae's humble, understated response ('I haven't done anything of note'). する + ておる is the humble form.
feedback.incorrect_en: やっては is too casual and doesn't match her formal register; できては is ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.jp: 大したことはしておりません。
contrast_examples.en: I haven't done anything of note. (humble)

contrast_examples.jp: 大したことはやってない。

prompt.context_jp: 自分の仕事を 軽く 低く考えるのは あまりにも自分に対して___
prompt.prompt_jp: あまりにも自分に対して___。

feedback.correct_en: 無責任 ('irresponsible') fits Omae's logic: belittling your own work is failing in your responsibility to yourself.
feedback.incorrect_en: 無関心 ('indifferent') and 無駄 ('wasteful') don't match the moral weight she's placing on self-accountability.

prompt.context_jp: あれは 昨日の段階で ___ 企画なので あのままです
prompt.prompt_jp: 昨日の段階で___企画なので、あのままです。

feedback.correct_en: 企画を捨てる = 'discard a proposal' is the natural collocation for actively killing a plan.
feedback.incorrect_en: 失う means 'to lose' something you didn't want to lose; 落とす means 'drop' — neither fits deliberately shelving a project.

prompt.context_jp: Omae firmly declining to do the presentation as a temp.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as Omae's polite refusal in a business context?

choices.text: プレゼンは派遣の仕事ではございません。
プレゼンは派遣の仕事じゃないよ。

feedback.correct_en: Omae's signature style is cold formal politeness. ではございません keeps the business register while firmly refusing.
feedback.incorrect_en: じゃないよ is far too casual for Omae addressing her manager during a client meeting.

contrast_examples.en: It is no concern of mine. (formal)

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka asking the team to pitch in on an impossible rush job.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'let's all pitch in somehow'?

choices.text: みんなで手分けして、何とか…
みんなで手を分けて、何とか…

feedback.correct_en: 手分けする is the fixed verb meaning 'divide up the work among people'. It's a single compound.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を分ける is a literal, awkward paraphrase that native speakers don't use for 'divide the work'.

prompt.context_jp: Asano casually thanking Chiba and Omae after the presentation success.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for Asano's casual, heartfelt thanks to subordinates?

choices.text: ホントに助かった。ありがとう。
本当に助けていただきました。ありがとうございます。

feedback.correct_en: Asano is senior speaking to junior/temp staff in a relaxed celebratory moment; ホントに助かった fits that warm, in-group register.
feedback.incorrect_en: The super-polite form would feel oddly stiff and over-formal from a senior toward his own subordinates.

contrast_examples.jp: 助かったよ、ありがとう。

contrast_examples.en: Thank you for your help. (formal, to outside)

prompt.context_jp: Omae rebuffing Ide's lumping her into the 'lonely' category.
prompt.prompt_en: Which matches Omae's characteristic blunt-polite register?

choices.text: 勝手に寂しいくくりにしないでください。
寂しいとか言わないでくれない？

feedback.correct_en: Omae uses formal teineigo even when scolding — 〜しないでください keeps her signature cold politeness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ないでくれない is casual/intimate and completely inconsistent with Omae's character throughout the show.

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka praising Omae's work on the revised proposal.
prompt.prompt_en: Which is more natural as a workplace compliment to a temp worker?

choices.text: 大前さん、ありがとうございます。素晴らしいです。
大前さん、サンキュー。すごいじゃん。

feedback.correct_en: Satonaka maintains teineigo with Omae — he respects her and the professional context. 素晴らしいです is appropriate praise.
feedback.incorrect_en: サンキュー・すごいじゃん is too casual for a section chief addressing a dispatch worker he barely knows personally.
